title: Austin Streets, Sidewalks, & A Forgiven Fine
summary:
*   **New Paved Streets and Sidewalks:** Approved final payments for significant street paving projects on Colorado and 9th Streets, and established new sidewalk lines on Congress Avenue, specifically ensuring space for existing trees.
*   **A Second Chance for a "Habitual Drunkard":** Forgave a court fine for Andy McQuirter, citing a judge's belief it would aid his reform, and noting the original payment had already been distributed to his wife and children.
*   **City Pays for Construction Damage:** Authorized funds to compensate property owners on Red River and 11th Street for damages caused by the city's changes to street grades during public works.
*   **Temporary Boost for Street Funds:** Approved a short-term $5,000 transfer from the Sanitary Sewer Earnings fund to support general street improvements, with an agreement to return the money by early 1914.

. Regular meeting; of the City Council : Austin, Texas, November 13, 1913.
. The Council was called to order by the Mayor : Roll called : Present Mayor Wooldridge,
Councilmen Anthony, Bartholomew, Haynes & Powell 5 Absent none.
The minutes of the last regular and subsequent recessed meetings were read and adopted.
The Mayor laid before the Council the following reports from City Officers: Assessor &
Collector, the Sexton, the Supt of Streets, Asst City Clerk, the Inspector Weights and
Measures, the Treasurer, which were read and ordered filed.
Councilman Powell offered the following resolution : A resolution finally accepting
pavement and improvement of Colorado street from the south curb line of 8th street to the
north property line of 9th street. Pavement C.F. 8th-9th
accepted
Whereas, the Supt of Streets and Public Improvements has filed his report with the City
Council to the effect that the Texas Bitulithic Company has completed the work of paving
and improving Colorado street from the south curb line of 8th street to the north property
line of 9th street under contract with the City and that said work has been fully done in
strict accordance with said contract and specifications adopted by the City ,therefore, Be
it resolved by the City Council of the City of Austin : That the said work of improvement
be finally accepted by the City and that the final estimate due by the City to the said
Company be paid.
The resolution was adopted by the following vote : Yeas Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen
Anthony, Bartholomew, Haynes & Powell 5 Nays none.
Councilman Powell offered the following resolution : Resolution finally accepting pavement
and improvement of 9th street from the west property line of Colorado street to the east
property line of Lavacca street.
Pavement 9th St. from
Colorado to Lavaca
accepted
Whereas, the Supt of Streets and Public Improvements has filed his report with the City
Council to the effect that the Texas Bitulithic Company has completed the work of paving
and improving 9th street from the west property line of Colorado street to the east
property line of Lavacca street under contract with the City and that said work has been
fully done in strict accordance with said contract and specifications adopted by the City;
Therefore, Be it resolved by the City Council of the City of Austin : That the said work
of improvement be finally accepted by the City and that the final estimate due by the City
to the said Company be paid.
The resolution was adopted by the following vote : Yeas Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen
Anthony, Bartholomew, Haynes & Powell 5 Nays none.
Councilman Anthony offered the following resolution : Be it resolved by the City Council
of the City of Austin : That the following transfers be and the same are hereby made of
the funds Transfer appropriation
dept. Police, etc.

The Mayor laid before the Council the following resolution : Be it resolved by the City
Council of the City of Austin : Sidewalk lines
Cong. Avenue 15th
To 16th St
✓
That the sidewalk on the east side of Congress Avenue between 15th & 16th streets be and
the same is hereby established parallel to the true property line and to the center line
of said Congress Avenue. The west line of the sidewalk located under this resolution shall
be so placed that it will in no instance be closer than twelve ( 12) inches to the east
line of the closest trees now located on the sidewalk of said block.
The resolution was adopted by the following vote : Yeas Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen
Anthony, Bartholomew, Haynes & Powell 5 Nays none.
Approved, A P Wooldridge, Mayor.
Councilman Anthony offered the following resolution : Be it resolved by the City Council
of the City of Austin : Andy McQuirter
Fine remitted
✓
That the fine and costs imposed upon Andy McQuirter ,in cause No 7963, in the Corporation
Court of the City of Austin, Texas, be and the same are hereby remitted, and the Clerk of
the Corporation Court declared to be intitled to take credit on his accounts accordingly.
The reasons moving the Council to remit the fine and costs in this case are that it
believes, upon information of the Judge of the Corporation Court ,that such action will
help to reform said Andy McQuirter,heretofore almost an habitual drunkard.
It is also here stated ,as a part of the moving cause to the Council for its action in
this matter , that the fine and costs in this cause' have already been paid by the
defendant McQuirter into the hands of the Clerk of the Corporation Court , and have by him
from time, to time, been turned over to the Wife and Children,.of said Defendant.
The resolution was adopted by the following vote: Yeas Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen
Anthony, Bartholomew, Haynes & Powell 5 Nays none.
Mayor Wooldridge offered the following resolution : Be it resolved by the City Council of
the City of Austin : Resolution to
temporary funds
repealed
✓
That the resolution of the City Council ,adopted Nov 11th, 1913, making a temporary
transfer of $ 5,000.00 from the Permanent Street Improvement fund to the General Street
Improvement fund be and the same is hereby repealed.
The resolution was adopted by the following vote : Yeas Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen
Anthony, Bartholomew, Haynes 4
Nays Councilman Powell 1
Mayor Wooldridge offered the following resolution : Be it resolved by the City Council of
the City of Austin : That a temporary transfer of five thousand ($ 5,000.00) dollars from
the Sanitary Sewer Earnings fund to the General Street Improvement fund is hereby made,
with the express understanding that this $ 5,000.00 so transferred ,shall, immediately
after the 1st day of January 1914, be transferred back from the General Street Improvement
fund to the

The Council then recessed subject to call.

November 18th 1913.
The Council was called to order by the Mayor with all members present: Councilman Powell
offered the following resolution: Be it resolved by the City Council of the City of
Austin: Repairs property of That seventy five (& 75.00) dollars, or so much thereof as may
be necessary, J L Costley be and is hereby appropriated out of the General Street
Improvement fund of the City of Austin, Texas, to pay for such repairs and improvements as
may be necessary, in the judgement of the Supt of Streets and Public Improvements, to be
made upon the property of J L Costley, at the corner of Red River and 11th street in this
City, growing out of change of grade in street made at that point by the City of Austin.
The resolution was adopted by the following vote: Yeas Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen
Anthony, Bartholomew, Haynes & Powell 5. Nays none.
Approved, A P Wooldridge, Mayor.
Councilman Powell offered the following resolution: Be it resolved by the City Council of
the City of Austin: For S Rosenberg That two hundred ($ 200.00) dollars or so much thereof
as may be necessary, be and is hereby appropriated out of the General Street Improvement
fund of the City of Austin, to make good conditions to the property of S Rosenberg,
brought about by change of grade by the City of Austin at the corner of 11th and Red
River streets in this City.
The resolution was adopted by the following vote: Yeas Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen
Anthony, Bartholomew, Haynes & Powell 5 Nays none.
Approved, A P Wooldridge, Mayor.
The Council then adjourned.
J F Wooldridge
City Clerk
